prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
No one can reliably pick stocks that beat the S&P 500 over a single year. In most years, most professional fund managers underperform it, and over 15 years roughly 9 in 10 do. Also, my knowledge ends in May 2026, so I don't have current prices, valuations, or recent earnings. Check those before acting.

With that in mind, here's a diversified list of 10 strong companies that are reasonable candidates to research. It mixes AI infrastructure, healthcare, financials, energy and a defensive holding.

## 10 Stock Ideas

| # | Company (Ticker) | Sector | Thesis | Key Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Semis | Makes nearly all of the most advanced AI chips (Nvidia, Apple, AMD, Broadcom). It isn't in the S&P 500, so it adds real diversification. | Geopolitical risk around Taiwan and China; tariffs |
| 2 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Semis | Custom AI chips for hyperscalers and data-center networking, plus steady software cash flow from VMware | High valuation; depends on a few large customers |
| 3 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Software / Cloud | Azure growth, AI tools built into Office and enterprise products, very strong balance sheet | Heavy AI spending may pressure margins |
| 4 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Internet / Cloud | Search cash flow, Google Cloud growth, Gemini, Waymo optionality; often cheaper than other megacaps | Antitrust remedies; AI chatbots disrupting search |
| 5 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | E-commerce / Cloud | AWS is the cloud leader, and advertising and retail margins keep improving | Consumer slowdown; AWS competition |
| 6 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Healthcare | Leader in GLP-1 obesity and diabetes drugs, with an oral pill pipeline and a huge addressable market | Premium valuation; drug pricing pressure; competition |
| 7 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Financials | Best-run large U.S. bank, diversified revenue, benefits from capital-markets activity | Credit cycle or recession; regulatory changes |
| 8 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Energy / Industrials | Gas turbines and grid equipment for fast-growing electricity demand from data centers | Priced for a lot of growth; execution risk |
| 9 | **MercadoLibre (MELI)** | E-commerce / Fintech | The "Amazon + PayPal" of Latin America with a long runway for growth | Currency swings (Argentina, Brazil); margin pressure |
| 10 | **Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B)** | Diversified | Defensive ballast with a large cash pile to deploy in a downturn | Leadership transition after Buffett; may lag in strong bull markets |

## How to Use This Wisely

1. **Consider a core-satellite approach.** Keep most of your money (say 70–80%) in an S&P 500 index fund and use the remaining 20–30% for picks like these. You get a shot at outperformance without betting everything on it.
2. **Understand the overlap.** Several of these (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, AVGO, JPM, LLY) are already big S&P 500 weights, so this basket may track the index fairly closely. Beating the index by a wide margin requires concentrated bets, which can also lose by a wide margin.
3. **Size positions sensibly.** Equal-weighting (about 10% each) is simple, and it helps not to let any one name grow past about 15%.
4. **Watch for AI concentration.** Five of the ten names depend heavily on the AI buildout, so a slowdown in AI spending would hit much of the list at once.
5. **Set a benchmark and review it honestly.** Compare your results against an S&P 500 fund such as VOO or SPY, including dividends, after 12 months.
6. **Mind taxes and fees.** Selling within a year triggers short-term capital gains, which can wipe out modest outperformance in a taxable account.

## Before You Buy

- Check each company's current valuation (P/E ratio and growth rate) and its latest earnings report, since things may have changed after May 2026.
- Only invest money you won't need for at least 3–5 years. One year is a very short and noisy horizon for stocks.
- For personalized advice based on your income, taxes and goals, a fee-only fiduciary financial advisor is worth considering.

If you tell me your risk tolerance, account type (taxable vs. retirement), and any sectors you prefer or want to avoid, I can tailor the list.
